turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Hi there, how are you feeling today?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I'm trying to figure out where I should study this semester.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Wait until I've listed everything before you jump in.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: One option is my bedroom desk, which is quiet but right next to my bed and my phone charger.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Another is the campus library, a twenty minute walk, but nobody bothers me there.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Or there's the coffee shop downstairs, a bit noisy, but I always feel weirdly focused there.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Right, um, that's everything, I think. Your thoughts?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: The library sounds like the best bet for deep work, the walk even gives you a little break. The coffee shop is great if the background noise actually helps you. Your bedroom is the riskiest, with the bed and phone so close.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Right, next thing. My best friend uses a wheelchair and I want to plan a day out on a trail together.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Lovely idea. Many parks now have accessible trails with smooth, firm surfaces and gentle slopes.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Look on the park or council website, they often list accessible routes with details on gradients, gates and toilets.
